clue.text: Prototype for 18 in private hell with mad bats?

indicators.note: someone who is bats is crazy, so the letters beside it are scrambled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tormented soul surrounded by crazed bats, the sort of scene that inspired a horror classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is DRACULA (18-down). 'Bats' suits the vampire theme but is the anagram signal; 'with' simply joins the two pieces of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker is often said to have drawn on the cruel Wallachian prince Vlad III when creating his Count, so he was the model.

clue.text: Is it 18 in burning heap we hear after 5am?

definitions.note: a question: is Count 18 one of these? He is

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the burning heap is respelt by its pronunciation
after places the sound-alike behind the time abbreviation in reading order

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written: the morning abbreviation
a pyre is a heap of wood for burning a body; spelt by how it sounds

explanation.surface: A question about whether some fiend is lurking in a funeral fire just after dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: VAMPIRE is V + AM + a sound-alike of PYRE. 18 is DRACULA (18-down).
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula is the most famous example of the blood-drinking undead, so asking whether he is one gives the category.

clue.text: Feline not caught by mammoth roaming free

indicators.note: not caught says the cricket abbreviation for caught is taken away from the cat word
by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: a feline is a cat
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
mammoth means huge

explanation.surface: A wild cat that eluded capture by a woolly mammoth wandering loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not caught' is cricket shorthand: C stands for caught on a scorecard, so that letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaped prisoner or animal still uncaptured is said to be at large, an idiom for being free.

clue.text: Small role reversed for mouse-catchers?

indicators.note: reversed tells us the combined letters are read from end to start

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: An actor given a tiny role that has been turned around, playing a cat perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousetraps are the devices used to catch mice, so traps fit as mouse-catchers.

clue.text: Lasting purpose united leaderless country

definitions.note: the noun sense: the act of lasting

indicators.note: without a leader means the first letter of the country is dropped

blocks.note: an end is an aim or purpose
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
the European country

explanation.surface: A political slogan about a nation without a head finding lasting unity and purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity for holding out over time, which is what lasting means as a noun.

clue.text: See 1
Absurd how Endgame ends?

blocks.note: the play title's final letter is E, so it finishes with preposition, article and that letter

explanation.surface: A wry dig at Beckett's Endgame, a famously absurdist play with a bleak finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase literally: the word Endgame ends 'in an E'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, a straightforward synonym of absurd.

clue.text: Revolutionary dance move?

blocks.note: surface reading: radical, as in political revolution
setter's reading: a ballet step that spins the dancer around

explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary suggests uprising, but here it simply means turning around.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet the dancer makes a full turn on one foot, a step involving a revolution of the body.

clue.text: Callas stimulated by a prestigious opera house

indicators.note: something stimulated is stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soprano Maria Callas inspired by performing at a famous venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Maria Callas sang many famous seasons at this Milan house, so the surface rings true.
explanation.definitionFit: The Teatro alla Scala in Milan is one of the world's most celebrated venues for opera.

clue.text: Despair's ending — two biblical characters give solace

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel
Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Bible figures bringing comfort to someone at the end of their despair.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to ease their distress, which is to comfort or console them.

clue.text: Old woman left with fat duck

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
L is the abbreviation for left
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: An elderly woman went off with a plump duck, perhaps for the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is slang for mother, giving MA.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck with the green-headed drake, a specific species of duck.

clue.text: Trained with Rosa, Leo can type

indicators.note: trained suggests being drilled into shape, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people, Rosa and Leo, learning to type, as if at secretarial school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can type' reads as able to use a keyboard; it is a kind of can.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised spray can, so it is one variety of can.

clue.text: Popular book set aside

blocks.note: something in is fashionable or popular
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A best-selling book being put aside for a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held in reserve is kept back for later use, which is what set aside means.

clue.text: American extended period in employment

blocks.note: US is short for American
an age is a long stretch of time

explanation.surface: Describing an American who has been in a job for many years.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the use or handling of something, matching employment in its sense of putting to use.

clue.text: Odds? Yes and no!

blocks.note: first reading: a betting price, and one-to-one is indeed such a price, so yes
second reading: odd numbers, and these are the opposite of odd, so no

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is both a betting price (odds) and the opposite of odd numbers, hence 'yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a one-to-one price is a type of odds, while in arithmetic the same word names non-odd numbers.

clue.text: Twenty on the job? Result!

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: a score is twenty
a line of work is a job

explanation.surface: Someone delighted at landing twenty jobs, or twenty years at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation makes 'Result!' sound like British slang for a win; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoreline is the final score of a match, i.e. its result.

clue.text: Horrifying experience in Black Horse?

blocks.note: night is black, as in black as night
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: Something terrifying happening at a pub called the Black Horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Horse looks like a pub name, a common one in Britain, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a frightening dream or, by extension, any terrible ordeal.

clue.text: Hop's wild with Great Balls of Fire?

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dancer going crazy to Jerry Lee Lewis's rock-and-roll hit Great Balls of Fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Great Balls of Fire is a song title, but 'Great' is fodder and only 'Balls of Fire' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot is a cluster of small iron balls fired from a cannon, so balls of fire in a literal sense.

clue.text: Stellar group with city lawyer

blocks.note: and means together with
the Italian capital city
DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A star-studded team of top advocates working with an urban law firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, and also names the nearest large galaxy, both groups of stars.

clue.text: Problem for which 18 potentially responsible?

blocks.note: surface reading: a nuisance or annoyance
setter's reading: the Count's bite at the throat would hurt in a literal sense

explanation.walkthrough: 18 is DRACULA (18-down). The idiom for an irritation is taken literally: a vampire bites the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an annoying person or thing, and a vampire's fangs would also cause literal soreness there.

clue.text: Doctor with a copper onto the French monster?

indicators.note: in a down clue, onto means placed on top of what follows

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
la is French for the (feminine)

explanation.surface: A doctor and a policeman closing in on some French fiend.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, but it is the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker's Count is a fictional vampire, a monster of Gothic horror.

clue.text: Go in chippy where there's no fish?

indicators.note: where there is none of it says the fish is taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: chippy is British slang for a carpenter, a woodworker
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Visiting a fish-and-chip shop that has run out of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is British slang for a fish-and-chip shop, the false picture, and also for a carpenter, the real sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to go into a place, a plain synonym.

clue.text: See 17
One no longer working on Hebridean island

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
Tiree is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped work and moved to a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiree has left employment for good, typically on reaching pension age.

clue.text: Top-class puzzle? Wow!

blocks.note: A is the top grade, as in A1
a maze is a puzzle of paths

explanation.surface: An excited reaction to an excellent puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wow!' looks like an exclamation but is the verb, meaning to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: To wow an audience is to astonish them, which is what amaze means.

clue.text: Change the last word daughter intended in speech

indicators.note: in speech means spoken, so the word for intended is respelt by its sound

blocks.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer
D is the abbreviation for daughter
meant means intended; spelt by how it sounds

explanation.surface: Someone altering the final word of a speech to what a daughter meant to say.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is an alteration, especially to a document or law, so it is a change.

clue.text: What's become of person, late, fired?

definitions.text: What's become of person, late, fired?

blocks.note: surface reading: an employee sacked for turning up late

blocks.clueFragment: What's become of person, late, fired?
blocks.note: setter's reading: what remains of a dead person after cremation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means deceased and 'fired' means burned, not tardy and sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremated remains are what is left after a body is burned, the late person's residue.

clue.text: You should take snuff!

blocks.note: a dose is the amount a patient should take
U sounds like you, as in text speak

explanation.surface: A recommendation to take some snuff, the powdered tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside DOSE. Snuff looks like tobacco but is the verb, to put out a candle.
explanation.definitionFit: To douse a flame is to extinguish it, just as you snuff out a candle.

clue.text: Feed on sour fish when starters are gone?

indicators.note: starters are the first letters, and with them gone each word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eating soured fish once the first course has been cleared away.
explanation.walkthrough: Starters suggests the opening dishes of a meal; here it means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to provide with food, a direct synonym for feed as a verb.

clue.text: Hot film director's arrogance

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an auteur is a director with a distinctive personal style

explanation.surface: A trendy filmmaker's haughty attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauteur is haughtiness or a lofty manner, which is a form of arrogance.

clue.text: Grooms devoured in North and South

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the two compass letters around it

blocks.note: devoured means eaten
N and S are the compass abbreviations

explanation.surface: Bridegrooms being eaten up across the whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: Grooms looks like a plural noun but is a verb, meaning tidies up.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom something is to make it smart and tidy, which is to neaten it.

clue.text: Kirk there regularly excited his fan?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
excited means stirred up, so the gathered letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Captain Kirk getting someone excited enough to become his devoted fan.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Kirk commands the Enterprise in Star Trek, so 'his fan' is a Star Trek devotee.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trekkie is an enthusiast of the Star Trek franchise, whose best-known hero is James T. Kirk.
